newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH KIDD SUMMONED TO MEETING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH KIDD SUMMONED TO MEETING.

text.p: Ireland coach Murray Kidd, beset by rumours that he faces the sack, has been summoned to a meeting with Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) officials on Tuesday, the union said in a statement on Monday.
The IRFU said the meeting would cover matters relating to the performance and the future preparation of the international team, who lost 37-29 to lowly Italy at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.
Irish media said on Monday that New Zealander Kidd was expected to be dismissed this week, following the mauling by Italy.
Since the start of last year's international championship, Ireland have lost six of seven matches under Kidd, including an embarrassing 40-25 defeat by Western Samoa.
Ireland team manager Pat Whelan said after the Lansdowne Road debacle on Saturday that Ireland's play was "devoid of any concerted or discernible pattern".
But Kidd himself said that as far as he was concerned there was no hint that he would be dismissed.
"I spoke to Pat (Whelan) on Sunday night and he told me to carry on with the preparations for the match against France. That is the situation as far as I am concerned," Kidd said.
Ireland host France in the first round of the Five Nations championship at Lansdowne Road on January 18.
Kidd, appointed Ireland's first full-time coach 15 months ago, acknowledged that the string of defeats had created pressure for himself and the side but ruled out resigning.
